summary: Discovery of a hole probably caused by a meteorite impact.
description: On December 25, 2004, a witness discovered a hole 15 cm in diameter and 25 cm deep in the parking lot of his property. Despite searching to a depth of 50 cm, no object was found. This hole was likely caused by a meteorite impact.

summary: A plausible observation of a celestial body.
description: On December 21, 2004, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness reported seeing a bright, shimmering point of light in the sky, its colors changing. This point remained stationary and silent, gradually rising in the sky. The observation was most likely that of a celestial body.

summary: A bright white ball of intense light descending towards the ground.
description: On December 1, 2004, at approximately 7:30 PM, a witness observed a very bright white ball in the sky descending at high speed. Before reaching the ground, this ball transformed into a small red dot and disappeared. Another witness, an off-duty soldier, also observed this phenomenon, which he thought resembled a flare. The witnesses likely observed atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a Boeing aircraft during its landing phase
description: On Thursday, November 25, 2004, a witness driving his car saw a triangular object estimated to be about ten meters in size. The object was stationary above the trees and had three fixed lights: white, red, and blue. The object then moved, causing the witness to flee the scene. He also heard no noise. The phenomenon was identified as a low-flying airliner on its landing approach, forced to make a loop before touching down. The triangle observed by the witness is, in all likelihood, the Boeing 737-8 as seen from a three-quarter rear angle.

summary: Observation of the very rapid rise of a bright point
description: On October 8, 2004, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness observed a bright point of light rising very rapidly and disappearing into the sky. The silent phenomenon lasted only about three seconds. No further information is available.

summary: Discontinuous observation by a motorist of unusual shapes in a very cloudy sky: lack of information.
description: On October 26, 2004, at approximately 2:15 PM, a motorist driving on the highway suddenly felt he was being watched. Turning his head, he was intrigued by the presence of gray, circular shapes in a cloud. These shapes moved like fan blades and reminded him of an eye. The observation was intermittent, lasting several seconds; the witness did not stop. Only one witness account was collected. The witness reported his observation three years later. The account lacks consistency, as: - the observation is detailed despite being from a long time ago and having occurred under less than ideal conditions, while driving at 130 km/h and looking behind him; The possibility of a reflection from the closed windows is not entirely ruled out, although mentioned and then dismissed by the witness. - The observation takes place in a highly emotional context induced by the feeling of being observed, a feeling present even before the observation, and which seems to lead to the retention of details or comparisons related to an "observing eye." Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information. Note: the witness made a similar observation (following a vehicle on the highway) two weeks earlier. Case AIX-EN-PROVENCE (13) 05.10.2004

summary: A Mirage patrol is briefly "followed" by unknown traffic.
description: On October 15, 2004, the leader of a Mirage 4 patrol was alerted by a wingman who reported being "followed" by an aircraft within the next five hours. The leader also visually identified the aircraft, which disappeared after 15 to 20 seconds. The leader concluded that a fighter jet had passed overhead, but no trace of it was detected by ground controllers. The event remains unexplained.

summary: Cylindrical object detaching from a property.
description: On October 6, 2004, between 11:00 PM and 11:30 PM, two witnesses observed a luminous phenomenon 150 meters from their home. The object was cylindrical, approximately 1 meter thick and 1.5 meters in circumference; dazzling white and red lights were also visible. The object slowly rose into the air, leaving a neighboring property where no trace of it was found. Taking an oblique trajectory, the object disappeared into the clouds. No further information was gathered about this phenomenon.

summary: Multiple observations under different conditions: lack of information.
description: In 2014, a witness reported several instances in October 2004 where, feeling observed (on the highway and then at home), he made various observations or findings. The testimony lacks consistency, in fact: - the observation accumulates many details despite being from some time ago and having taken place under unsuitable conditions, while driving at 130 km/h and looking behind him; the hypothesis of a reflection from closed windows is not entirely ruled out, although mentioned and rejected by the witness. - the observation occurred within a strong emotional context induced by the feeling of being observed, a feeling present even before the observation, and which seems to lead to retaining details or comparisons related to an "observing eye." The witness recounts other situations involving emotions or strange occurrences linked to this sensation of being observed, even though these are not related to the presence or observation of UFOs. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observations of a luminous ball falling in the sky: probable observations of an atmospheric reentry.
description: On September 24, 2004, at approximately 7:30 a.m., a witness in their garden saw a luminous ball "fall" followed by a blue trail. Several witnesses reported this event, which was covered in the local press and identified as an atmospheric reentry of a meteor.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation. Observation by a motorist of a stationary object in the sky and sudden disappearance: lack of information.
description: In January 2012, GEIPAN received a questionnaire regarding an observation made on September 17, 2004, at 8:15 PM. On that day, a motorist on the D78 between Molières and Lafraneaise thought she saw a powerful light in the sky, but passing through Lafraneaise interrupted her vision. Leaving the village and overlooking the plain, the witness suddenly saw a stationary object. The witness stopped on a bend; the witness described a motionless, round object with two powerful headlights, each bordered on both sides by several lights. Fearing she would obstruct traffic, she moved forward. The object had disappeared by the time she raised her head. Only one witness statement was collected. The observation is described as strange: a vision of a motionless, round object with headlights, and its sudden disappearance. However, this testimony was given eight years after the sighting. The witness offers no explanation for the delay in reporting such a strange observation (the witness says, "I was both shocked and completely overwhelmed because my dearest wish was finally coming true: to witness an extraterrestrial phenomenon"). Yet, the level of shock from the sighting did not prevent him from reporting, since he "considered going to the police station the next day, but it was closed." Beyond the reluctance to report, the testimony contains its own inconsistencies: the date is inconsistent (from September 17 to October 17, 2004). The witness is drawn to one or two lights around which he then distinguishes a row of lights, but the subsequent drawings depict rows of lights without a main beam. One drawing represents an enormous saucer that occupies a large part of the witness's field of vision, but the witness did not see the disappearance. He was indeed busy restarting his car, but there is no mention of what the passenger might have seen regarding this disappearance, a passenger whom the witness nevertheless identifies as relevant to his testimony through the use of "we" and is described as being able to confirm everything. The consistency of the testimony is insufficient to render this observation, the account of which is strange, unexplained. This old and delayed testimony is unusable. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of high-speed, scintillating luminous phenomena.
description: During the night of August 15-16, 2004, a man standing on his balcony twice observed luminous, golden, and shimmering phenomena in a clear sky, moving at high speed. The first time, around 3:50 a.m., the lights moved in a triangular pattern; the second time, around 4:20 a.m., they were in a line and on the same trajectory as before. It should be noted that the area was near Lille-Lesquin Airport. No further information could be gathered about this observation, which was classified as a Category C event.

summary: Observation of the straight passage of nine white lights in the sky outlining a dark mass; date of the day imprecise: lack of information.
description: witness reported to us in March 2015 an observation made around August 20th to 25th, 2004, while he was a front-seat passenger in a vehicle. Near the exit for Saint-Maximin-la-Sainte-Baume (83), the witness observed through the windshield the passage of nine white lights that seemed to outline a large, dark mass. The trajectory was straight. Only one witness account was collected. Given the position and appearance of the Moon described by the witness (full Moon, to the right of the highway, high in the sky), this observation must have occurred on August 26th, 27th, 28th, or 29th (see star charts). The appearance and behavior of the phenomenon described by the witness suggest an airplane at low altitude, with all lights on, preparing for landing. We note that the witness was observing very close to the OGREN aeronautical reference point (see map), which serves as a reference point for the approach path to Marignane aerodrome, located 50 km away. He therefore frequently sees aircraft flying at medium or low altitude, with all lights on, passing over this area. The witness, focused on the landing lights, may have missed the less powerful flashing lights. It is surprising, however, that the witness could have made such a mistake, given his experience in the aeronautical field; but one does not have the same reference points and reflexes outside of a professional context. This aircraft hypothesis cannot, however, be verified due to the uncertainty surrounding the date and, above all, the more than 10-year gap between the events and the witness's testimony. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C" due to a lack of information.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation. Brief observation of the silent movement above the vineyards and cars of the A5 motorway of a yellow circular phenomenon: lack of information and cross-checking.
description: Recent report (May 2015) of a previous sighting. The witness recounts an observation made probably in July or August 2004 around 1:40 PM on the D6009 after Prat-de-Cest (11) in the commune of Peyriac-de-Mer. While driving, the witness saw a circular yellow object approaching the left corner of their windshield at low altitude. The driver stopped and saw a yellow disc cross the D6009 to the side of the road, moving towards the A9 motorway less than a meter above the green vines without disturbing them. Crossing the motorway, the object moved vertically, then resumed a horizontal trajectory, flying over the cars and then over an embankment. The witness lost sight of the object, which was hidden by the motorway embankment. The object appeared to originate from the Doule ponds to the east and move westward. No unusual noises were noticed during the observation. No other testimonies were collected. This observation is considered moderately to highly unusual, as it describes a similar phenomenon and atypical behavior (see investigation notes). The case is not highly consistent: it consists of a single witness, old memories, and, most importantly, the precise date is unknown, making any meteorological verification impossible. The only hypothesis considered, ball lightning, is not sufficiently substantiated to be accepted. This case is ultimately classified as C due to a lack of dated information and corroborating evidence.

summary: Observations of the movement of luminous points outlining a dark triangular shape with a muffled engine noise: probable observations of an airplane.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-HAON LE CHATEL (42) 2004, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. Two witnesses reported their sighting to a UFO association and the press before being summoned to the gendarmerie. They report that upon returning from a party on May 21, 2004, around 1:30 or 2:00 AM, T1 observed a flashing, moving point of light in the sky. The two witnesses then observed this point of light following various trajectories (ascent, descent). The UFO approached, and the witnesses then distinguished several points of light of varying colors, all surrounding a triangular black mass. The witnesses heard a muffled engine noise. The phenomenon passed overhead at low altitude and then moved away towards the mountains. Although some data is missing (angle measurements, particularly altitude above the horizon and dimensions of the UFO, and the exact location of the colored lights on the UFO), and other data appears contradictory, key parameters allow for the hypothesis of a case of mistaken identity, probably involving a small private aircraft flying VFR at night (see the investigation report). These parameters consist of: - the presence, in the vicinity and along the observation line, of Roanne airport, approved for night VFR flights; - the direction of movement of the UFO towards other airports on the other side of the mountain; - the perception by witnesses of an engine noise similar to that of an airplane or helicopter; - as well as three colors (red, green, yellow) conforming to aviation regulations. The elements that could be put against this hypothesis are: - Insufficient to invalidate the hypothesis: the plane may also have carried a blue light, made an irregular trajectory at the beginning or the perception of irregularity may have resulted from a natural physiological phenomenon of micro-mobility of the eye (micro-nystagmus) which occurs when one stares at a point of light, particularly at night and gives the false impression that point-like luminous objects are affected by small aberrant movements. - And/or tainted by a lack of reliability (e.g., blue light, changing lights) due firstly to the conditions of observation (strong emotion, generated from the outset by an extreme hypothesis of an object connected to the witnesses, or even an extraterrestrial object, which could alter the perception or memorization of certain factors observed subsequently) and secondly to the conditions of testimony (summoned by the gendarmerie, after initial disclosure to a journalist). The consistency of the testimonies is weak: - Lack of information. No measurements of angular dimensions were taken, nor were the exact locations of the colored lights observed by the witnesses on the UFO specified. - Reliability is compromised by the conditions of observation (see above) as well as by the conditions of testimony. Nevertheless, the case can be classified as B: probable observation of an aircraft. Borderline as a C case: unusable testimony.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On May 20, 2004, at approximately 12:30 a.m., a witness and their partner observed a silent shape moving at very high speed without making any noise from their terrace. A powerful beam of light was visible at the rear of the shape, while the front was green. The shape slowed down, the beam faded, leaving only the green light before disappearing completely. The observation lasted three to four minutes. Following a press article, a second witness, an amateur astronomer, came forward. He observed the phenomenon for several tens of seconds and interpreted it as atmospheric reentry. The phenomenon was classified as Class B, as the hypothesis of atmospheric reentry was accepted.

summary: Observation of the movements of an intense point of light crossing the sky in a few minutes: observation of ISS passes.
description: On May 14, 2004, at 9:44 PM, an amateur astronomer observed a very bright point of light moving slowly from southwest to northeast in the sky for a few minutes. The object made a second pass on a different trajectory, but still towards the northeast, at 11:30 PM. The witness, an amateur astronomer, was intrigued by this phenomenon, which he could not explain. No other witness statements were collected by the gendarmerie, and this case, formerly known as CERET (60), was classified as a C case by the SEPRA (Specialized Investigation and Research Service). Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience acquired over the past few years, a re-examination of this case was possible (see the document "Investigation Notes"). The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, movement, etc.) with a well-known spacecraft: the International Space Station (ISS), which was indeed present on the indicated trajectory and at the times provided by the witness. The witness's visual perception is not the issue, but rather their interpretation of the observation, stemming from a misconception that satellites could not have been visible at the time of the observation. In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak anomaly is classified as UAP A, an observation of ISS passes.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On May 10, 2004, at approximately 9:20 PM, two independent witnesses observed the very rapid passage of a luminous yellow-orange sphere. Although the two accounts are not entirely consistent regarding the movement (horizontal for one witness and vertical for the other), there is little doubt that the witnesses observed atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations two nights in a row with the naked eye then with binoculars and a camcorder of yellow and green balls shining intensely in the night sky and with pereus movements: probable observations of Venus.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named DIJON (21) 2004, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On May 2, 2004, around 11:30 PM, and again on May 3, around 8:30 PM, a witness and his son observed a luminous phenomenon that intrigued them for a considerable time, first with the naked eye, then with binoculars, and finally by recording a video. Witnesses describe the presence in the sky of luminous orbs of color much larger than the surrounding stars. These orbs appear to move away and then approach before disappearing rapidly. The light intensity is very high. The description includes characteristics typical of a celestial object sighting: - the observation period is long (> 15 or 30 minutes) and the UFO changes little or not at all in position in the sky. - the UFO appears two nights in a row with a sufficiently identical appearance and position for the witness to report it as the same phenomenon. (T1: "The following evening around 10:30 PM, I filmed this phenomenon again"). The indication of the second night (Moon opposite the direction) establishes the direction of observation as NW. Now, in the NW, a star much brighter than the others predominates: Venus. - T1 said, "I went to the window and that's when I saw a large, luminous ball in the sky, ten times bigger than a star. It was green." - T2 said, "My father called me and said, 'Come see, there's a star bigger than the others.' I looked and saw a large yellow and green star." It is clear that, despite the weather report indicating cloudy skies, the witnesses observed a group of stars in that direction of the sky, since T2 said, "I want to clarify that there were several stars that evening, but this ball was bigger than the others." All of the above is characteristic of a misunderstanding regarding Venus, which is indeed much brighter (or "larger") than other stars and, above all, can appear in varied and changing colors due to atmospheric effects, which can also create sensations of movement (T2 said, "This phenomenon also zigzagged from right to left and up and down"). The strange elements described by the witnesses initially amount to the sighting of a star that was unusual in its intensity and its yellow or green color. Then, there is a distinct increase in perceived strangeness with these other spheres accompanying the main sphere, the latter also making back-and-forth movements (T1: "this sphere resembles a tennis ball, constantly moving, rapidly approaching and moving away," "other luminous spheres formed above, creating a "V" shape and descending rapidly to the level of the village lights. Then, these spheres moved away just as quickly."). That evening, Venus, with Saturn and Mars on one side, and Elnath and Capella on the other, formed a V pointing downwards towards Venus (see the reconstruction document). The whole assembly does indeed descend (as described) towards the city lights, passing (on the first day) from the 10th elevation at 11:30 PM to cross the horizon to the right at 12:40 AM. T2 says, "Then later there was a ball that came back with another smaller one." This could correspond (see reconstruction) to Pollux and Castor, who indeed take the initial place of Venus. The perception of back-and-forth movement for T1, or for T2 of "leaving and returning," or even of "rapid movement eastward" (that is, approaching T2 since it is facing northwest), could correspond to a well-known optical illusion from GEIPAN: variations in the intensity of a UFO, here caused by variations in atmospheric opacity, are interpreted as changes in the distance of the UFO. It should be noted that this increased perceived strangeness (beyond the initial appearance of the yellow star) begins with observation through binoculars and especially on the video. From then on, it becomes difficult to distinguish what results from observation with the naked eye and what results from observation via a device. And this is probably This added layer of strangeness led witnesses to testify and may also have led GEIPAN to initially classify the case as unexplained D. However, we now know from experience that strange phenomena perceived in videos, photos, or with binoculars, which are not already minimally visible to the naked eye, are in the vast majority of cases artifacts from these devices—artifacts that generate a very strong perception of strangeness. Furthermore, GEIPAN no longer considers these types of testimonies. GEIPAN does not have the video transmitted to the gendarmerie to proceed with confirmation. The V-shaped object explained above by the astronomical configuration has a wingspan of 30 arcseconds and would correspond more closely to a naked-eye view, but it is possible that the V is much smaller and was perceived only in the video, and is a pure video artifact related to the zoom (maximum here). It is also possible that the video artifact(s) created a strong feeling of strangeness. This strangeness then led to the perception of an astronomical configuration as strange to the naked eye, a configuration that was only moderately strange to begin with (a large yellow or green star). Although the exact origin of this increased strangeness cannot be determined between the two plausible causes (astronomical configuration or instrument artifact), it is clear that the starting point of the observation is very likely Venus, and that without the use of instruments, the strangeness would have remained limited to this star, which is larger than the others and yellow in color. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observations of Venus.

summary: 2004. Observations of the slow movement of a very bright point in the middle of a cluster of stars: observations of a rare configuration (every eight years) of the planet Venus in the middle of the Pleiades cluster.
description: On the night of April 2, 2004, several witnesses observed a bright point of light in the west, very bright among the stars. At the scene, the police determined that the point was located approximately 30 arcseconds above the horizon and appeared to be moving very slowly. The police investigation revealed that the observed point was Venus seen among a cluster of stars known as the Pleiades, often mistaken for the Little Dipper. This phenomenon is rare and occurs approximately every eight years. The case is classified as Class A: Venus sightings.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On February 14, 2004, at approximately 3 p.m., numerous witnesses observed a luminous object falling. Given the characteristics and duration of the observation (a few seconds), it was likely an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Probable observation of a meteorite fall
description: On February 8, 2004, shortly before 7 p.m., a bright, red, rapidly falling object was observed. It was probably a meteorite.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On January 4, 2004, at approximately 5:45 PM, several witnesses observed a large fireball falling very rapidly. It was likely an atmospheric reentry.
